title: Minnisais (Liberty Island)
summary: Minnisais is a Chippewa name applied by Henry R. Schoolcraft to Bedlow's Island, now Liberty Island. It is included here as a later introduced name, not an older local placename from Long Island or New York Harbor records.
history_content: Minnisais connects a real New York Harbor island, a later introduced Native-language name, and a caution about mistaking such names for older local placenames.
translation_content:
The name is given as Minnisais and translated as the lesser island. It is described as a Chippewa form rather than a local Long Island or New York Harbor Indigenous placename.

Why Place Names Matter

“Learning Indigenous place names is a way to orient oneself, not just geographically but also culturally and historically. It is a way to challenge colonial power structures and contribute to a more just and inclusive world.”

— Ekaterina Mikhailova, The Importance of Indigenous Place Names (2025), concluding quotation
whereintheworld_content: Location note: The pin is placed at modern Liberty Island, historically Bedlow's Island, to represent the island to which Schoolcraft applied the name. It is not an exact historic coordinate for an event or boundary.
